evals.prompt: I want to build a self-hosted app that creates editable PowerPoint presentations with AI. Before we start coding, tell me whether there is anything on GitHub worth using as a base.
evals.expected_output: Live repository research with several credible candidates, verified evidence for key gates, and one explicit USE, CONTRIBUTE, FORK, or BUILD verdict before implementation begins.
assertions: The response performs repository discovery before proposing implementation
The response distinguishes discovery signals such as stars from verified fit and maintenance evidence
The response ends with exactly one primary USE, CONTRIBUTE, FORK, or BUILD verdict and a confidence level

evals.prompt: We need a self-hosted feature-flag service for an internal platform. It must have an API, auditability, active maintenance and a license we can use commercially. Compare reusing an existing open-source project with building our own.
evals.expected_output: A requirements-led shortlist that verifies license, maintenance, operational/security fit and adoption cost, then compares reuse with greenfield and selects one primary decision path.
assertions: The response treats the stated requirements as gates rather than ranking repositories primarily by popularity
The response verifies or marks unknown consequential license and maintenance claims
The response compares adoption or adaptation effort with greenfield effort

evals.prompt: Write me a ten-line bash script that renames every .jpeg file in this folder to .jpg.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes this as a trivial/throwaway script where full repository due diligence would add more cost than value, and does not force a multi-repository research cycle.
assertions: The response does not force a 3-6 repository due-diligence comparison for this tiny task
The response remains useful rather than refusing the task because discovery was unnecessary

evals.prompt: Do not browse or search GitHub. I know alternatives exist, but for this prototype I deliberately want a fresh implementation from scratch.
evals.expected_output: The skill respects the explicit instruction to skip discovery, states that the reuse gate is intentionally bypassed, and does not invent evidence about repositories it did not inspect.
assertions: The response honors the explicit request not to browse
The response does not fabricate repository comparisons or live GitHub evidence
The response makes clear that the reuse decision gate was intentionally bypassed
